items.title: Randy Rainbow Dissects the Midterm Blue Wave, Decimates Trump’s Second Term On ‘He’s a Flop!’: ‘He’s the Schmo Most Hated’
items.summary:
Randy Rainbow is never at a loss for words when it comes to launching tuneful, comedic broadsides against the man he affectionately refers to as “Donald Jessica Trump.” In his latest parody video, “He’s a Flop!,” Rainbow leans into a classic comedic trope to dance on Trump’s flaming pile of disasters by making it look like he’s on the other side of a serious, 60 Minutes -style interview on the news program he’s renamed 60 Magats .

Related 

51 Times Parody Singer Randy Rainbow Roasted Donald Trump 

Randy Rainbow Slams President Trump’s ‘Corpse-Like Appearance’ in Toe-Tapping ‘Oklahoma!’ Parody 

Randy Rainbow Drags ‘Dumbf–k Tyrant’ Donald Trump in Jazzy Song Parody Amid Iran War Discontent 

The six-minute video uses footage from a Trump interview about how he asked his MAGA faithful to pretend he was on the ballot before Democrats made historic gains in Congress and flipped both the House and Senate in a stinging rebuke of Trump’s agenda. “Well, you did manage to flip the whole damn country and now everyone’s distancing themselves from you,” Rainbow says. “Republicans, your stylist … obviously.”

Eventually, Rainbow gets to the heat of the meat, telling Trump that if you set aside the rising inflation, the tariffs, the sky-high grocery prices, the healthcare cuts, the ICE raids, the Epstein files disaster, “the wars, the corruption, the incompetence your overall proclivity for f–king everything up,” he thinks No. 47 is No. 1.

“At presidenting he’s unrelenting that he does it the very best/ To find one better you’d be hard-pressed,” Rainbow croons over subtle piano as…
items.t: Randy Rainbow Dissects the Midterm Blue Wave, Decimates Trump’s Second Term On ‘He’s a Flop!’: ‘He’s the Schmo Most Hated’

items.title: Drake Shot Future’s ‘Ya Hit’ Video Scenes at Moody Center Without Permission, Rice University Says
items.summary:

Related

According to Chron , Drizzy’s appearance on the Houston school grounds was unauthorized and campus security was left in the dark about the 6 God showing up.

“Neither the Moody Center for the Arts nor Rice University was aware of or involved in the production of Drake’s music video,” Rice’s executive director of news and media relations, Chris Stipes, told Chron . “While commercial filming on campus requires prior authorization, we recognize the broad appeal of the Rice Public Art Collection and welcome visitors to experience these remarkable works.”

However, the university isn’t pursuing any action against Drake for not securing permits and welcomes him back to the Moody Center for the Arts exhibits. “Drake, like all visitors, is welcome to return to campus to enjoy Rice’s public art,” Stipes continued. 

Billboard has also reached out to Drake, Future and Rice University for comment.

items.title: Travis Kelce Celebrates 100th Game at Arrowhead Stadium With Taylor Swift-Coded Comment: ‘It’s Pretty Awesome’
items.summary:
Travis Kelce has plenty of great memories playing at the Kansas City Chiefs’ home stadium. In fact, on Sunday (Nov. 22), three-time Super Bowl champ Kelce marked a new career milestone in his 14-year journey with the team when he became just the fourth player in franchise history to play 100 regular-season games at Arrowhead.

He discussed that major stat on this week’s episode of his New Heights podcast with brother Jason Kelce, including passing former Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski in total career touchdowns (110-to-108) and why his good memories also, of course, include ones tied to his wife Taylor Swift .

“One hundred games, dude, it feels pretty awesome right now,” Travis said of his home game high point. “To think about that legacy of that stadium, man and it’s pretty crazy to think they’re moving on from that stadium, because of all the history that’s happened over the years and history of the franchise and everything.” The Chiefs have announced plans to leave Arrowhead when their lease expires after the 2030 NFL season.

Then Travis dug into what it’s been like playing at Arrowhead all those years, adding a subtle nod to Swift, whose Eras Tour touched down at the stadium on July 7 and 8, 2023; Kelce was in attendance on night two.

“You know it’s been home for me for 14 years, and it’s been one of my favorite places to go to play and to watch not only football, but musical events and I’ve had so much history and so many things that mean so much to me happen at Arrowhead that a hundred games, it’s pretty awesome to hit that milestone,” Kelce said in a subtle…
items.t: Travis Kelce Celebrates 100th Game at Arrowhead Stadium With Taylor Swift-Coded Comment: ‘It’s Pretty Awesome’

The video found her in and out of auditions for a panel of overly critical men, changing things about her appearance and personality each time in futile attempts to please them.

By the end of the video, Grande realizes that none of those things should matter, and that the focus should have always been on her art. items.title: 2027 ACM Awards Changes Include New Criteria for New Artist Categories & Song of the Year
items.summary:
The Academy of Country Music Awards have amended criteria for a number of categories for both its artist and industry awards. Additionally, the ACM has finalized the submission and voting timeline for the 62nd ACM Awards, which will take place May 16 in Las Vegas.

For the artist awards, the changes include broadening the criteria for the new artist of the year awards, which are presented in new male, new female and new duo or group categories. The wording has been altered to “presented to a country music individual artist, duo, or group who gains initial notoriety and demonstrates significant creative growth and development in overall consumption or chart activity, live performance, and/or national media recognition during the eligibility period,” according to the official description of the award.

Related 

Here’s the Date of the 2027 ACM Awards – And How to Get Tickets 

Here Are the 2026 ACM Awards Winners: Full List 

Every 2026 ACMs Performance, Ranked 

Previously, a more restrictive definition noted that the recognition occurred “during the promotion of a debut or sophomore album within the eligibility period,” and specifically defined chart activity as “must have released a single that reached the top 50 on Billboard’s Hot Country Songs or the Mediabase Country charts.” Significantly, the new definition removes the album requirement in a nod to how release patterns have changed to focus on consumption. A qualifier that any albums self-released through an independent label operated by the artist would not be counted as a debut or sophomore album unless it produced…
items.t: 2027 ACM Awards Changes Include New Criteria for New Artist Categories & Song of the Year

Nashville-based music promoter Peachtree Entertainment, the organizer behind the Rock The Country festivals, has reportedly shut down and laid off staffers. The news was first reported by Decibel .

A statement released Friday (Nov. 20) to Loudwire from the city of Decatur, Ala., which hosted Rock The South, noted that the city had “received word that Peachtree Entertainment has decided to cease operations and close its business. This was a significant and unexpected development for City leadership.”

In the statement, the City of Decatur also noted it is reviewing its five-year agreement with Peachtree Entertainment and “assessing what this decision means for Decatur and the future of Rock the South.”

The statement added, “Because the review is ongoing, the City cannot confirm 2027 festival or event dates at this time. We can say that no city funds have been exchanged for the 2027 contract year. We understand that residents, local businesses, festival fans and community partners will have questions. The City will share additional information once we have verified facts and a clearer understanding of the available next steps.”

Representatives for Peachtree Entertainment have not responded to Billboard ‘s request for comment.

items.title: Jungle announce run of huge summer 2027 UK shows
items.summary:
Jungle have announced a run of massive UK shows for next summer, including a headline slot at Latitude .

READ MORE: Jungle interview: “I spent three years trying to make another ‘Busy Earnin’” 

The dates come in support of the BRIT-award winning trio dropping their uplifting fifth album ‘ Sunshine ’ earlier this year – their first since 2023’s ‘ Volcano ’.

Dates kick off at Bristol’s Queen Square on June 19 and will be one of the first concerts held at the outdoor space since Massive Attack performed a landmark set there in 2003. For over two decades there were no shows held there, until IDLES hosted a huge Block Party there last summer.

Jungle’s performance will follow the same sustainable initiative that IDLES had in place, becoming one of the first large-scale events of their kind in the UK to be powered entirely by batteries and the national grid, without a generator in sight.

View this post on Instagram 

The group have also been confirmed as a headliner for Latitude 2027, which returns to Henham Park in Southwold between July 22 and 25. It will be their first slot there since playing on the Second Stage back in 2014, and the other two headliners will be confirmed at a later date.

“We’re super excited to be heading back to Latitude in 2027,” the trio shared. “It’s one of the first festivals we ever played in the UK and to be asked to headline the Obelisk Arena next summer is an honour and we can’t wait.”

On July 25, they’ll perform at Brighton’s On The Beach festival, joining Two Door Cinema Club , Tom Jones , Pete Tong and more as headliners, and on July 31…

items.title: Andy Burnham says UK government have “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”
items.summary:
Andy Burnham has addressed the issues facing artists across the UK, and said that the government has “negotiated language that may make it easier in future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

READ MORE: UK touring bands are suffering due to “Brexit fuck-ups and a lack of government control” 

The Prime Minister made the comments in parliament, highlighting the widespread issues facing musicians looking to tour, including rising costs and Brexit – the latter of which putting an end to visa-free travel for UK artists and crew wishing to work and creating an existential threat to the talent pipeline .

Speaking about “touring musicians and artists”, Burnham said that he was “particularly pleased” that his parliament had “negotiated language that may make it easier in the future for British bands, performers and artists to tour in Europe”.

Addressing the threats facing the sector, he said that music is “arguably our finest export”, but also “an area we are in danger of taking too much for granted”.

“British music is known and loved around the world. Brexit made it harder to tour, but we now have a chance to explore mutually beneficial solutions,” he added. “We still have work to do, but let me say directly to all our musicians, I fully intend to take this opportunity.”

Burnham’s comments addressing the touring situation for artists following Brexit comes as he attended a major summit in Brussels on Friday (November 20), where the EU and UK announced a new UK–EU “reset” deal that affected food and drink, emissions trading and a youth mobility…

He then shared an update in October 2025, saying that he would be taking a “planned break” from the shows and sitting out the band’s dates in Asia and Australia so that he could get “the next phase of care”. He later rejoined them for shows in South America towards the end of the year.

In his absence, Noel Gallagher arranged for a life-sized cardboard version of Bonehead to be made to join the group on tour. Now, Bonehead has signed the cut-out and teamed up with The Christie Charity to auction it off for charity. All proceeds will support cancer care and research at The Christie NHS Foundation Trust in Manchester – the hospital that treated him with both his diagnoses.

items.title: Matthew Perry’s grave headstone ‘Friends’ reference removed
items.summary:
The plaque on Matthew Perry ’s headstone has been updated to remove a reference to Friends .

Matthew Perry was found unresponsive in a hot tub in his Los Angeles home on October 28, 2023. He was later pronounced dead, with his death being attributed to the acute effects of ketamine , and drowning and coronary artery disease listed as other factors.

Earlier this year, Perry’s live-in assistant Kenneth Iwamasa was sentenced to three years and five months in jail after being found guilty of injecting the Friends star with ketamine after working with two doctors to secure $50,000 (£38,000) of the drug in the weeks leading up to his death.

Jasveen Sangha, the drug dealer also known as the ‘Ketamine Queen’, was sentenced to 15 years in prison for supplying the drugs that Perry took before his death while rehab counsellor Erik Fleming, Dr. Salvador Plasencia and Dr. Mark Chavez were also found guilty of supplying Perry with ketamine .

As reported by Entertainment Weekly , a new grave marker was placed on Perry’s grave in January that read: “Matthew Langford Perry. August 19, 1969 – October 28, 2023. Much Loved – Friend –”.

Recently though, that plaque has been replaced. The new headstone still features Perry’s full name but now reads “Rest now. We love you with our whole hearts”.

'Friends' star Matthew Perry's grave marker no longer references his 'Friends' role.

The new plaque at Forest Lawn Hollywood Hills replaces the "Much Loved, Friend" marker, which now reads "Rest Now" followed by "We Love You With Our Whole Hearts."

READ MORE: “It felt like we were changing the world”: inside New Order’s seminal ‘Power, Corruption & Lies’ 

The gig took place on Monday (November 23) as the first date of the band’s 2026 tour of South America, and the first of their two 8,000 capacity shows in Sao Paulo, Brazil.

Kicking off slightly later than usual due to severe weather, the gig was the first full gig since Gillian Gilbert announced that she would not be joining the group on the road due to health reasons. It was also the first full New Order show without drummer Stephen Morris, who has stepped back from international touring.

Morris was the drummer in Joy Division alongside Bernard Sumner , Peter Hook and Ian Curtis , and the remaining members formed New Order with Gilbert after Curtis’ death in 1980. Morris and Gilbert have also released music together outside New Order as The Other Two. Their debut album, ‘The Other Two & You’, arrived in 1993, followed by ‘Super Highways’ in 1999.

In June, New Order confirmed that both Morris and Gilbert would not be touring with them in the “foreseeable future” due to “personal” reasons, and in September, Gilbert told fans that she is living with cancer .

items.title: The Beatles’ new London 3 Savile Row plans approved by council – with “truly immersive experience” planned for rooftop
items.summary:
New plans for The Beatles ’ London 3 Savile Row have been approved by the council, and include a “truly immersive experience” taking place on the rooftop.

READ MORE: Paul McCartney interviewed: “Writing a song is still a magic feeling for me, and hopefully always will be” 

The site was the Apple Corps headquarters in London, and the place where ‘ Let It Be ‘ was recorded. It also was the spot where they played their iconic final public performance in 1969 on the rooftop.

Earlier this year, the company announced it was converting the building into a seven-floor “cultural experience and exhibition” celebrating The Beatles, with a basement café-bar on the site of the studio where they recorded their last album.

It is set to open its doors next year and include seven floors of never-before-seen material from Apple Corps’ extensive archives, rotating exhibitions, a fan store, and a recreation of the original studio where ‘Let it Be’ was recorded. An expected 900 visitors are expected to visit each weekday, and around 1,140 on the weekends – although it was recently confirmed that no live music can be played on the terrace and any amplified music or speech will have to be limited.

Now, it has been confirmed that the plans for 3 Savile Row have been given the seal of approval from the government, and include a “truly immersive experience” that will take place on the rooftop.

The Westminster City Council’s Planning Committee approved the plans last night (Tuesday November 24), confirming that fans will be able to visit the exhibitions, the basement recording studio, and the…

items.title: ‘My name was poison’: Donny Osmond on fame, failure – and his friend Michael Jackson

He was the child star of the Osmonds who become a global celebrity by 14. Then, at 21, his career came crashing down. Here, he reveals how he survived his years in exile – and what happened when Jackson was accused of child abuse

For a brief period in the early 1970s, Donny Osmond ruled the world. He was the global teenage heart-throb. Even Michael Jackson trailed behind him. He was 14 when his most famous song, Puppy Love, spent five weeks at No 1 in the UK. My sister had a huge poster of him on her bedroom wall. Then again, everybody’s sister had a poster of him on their bedroom wall. Between 1972 and 1973 he had six Top 5 hits in the UK, three of them No 1s (including The Twelfth of Never and Young Love). He was equally successful back home in the US.

Osmond was clean-cut, religious and respectful, with a mighty ability to punch out cover versions of saccharine standards. From his purple velvet cap to his doleful eyes and dazzling all-American smile, he was a marketing dream. We’d only just finished with Beatlemania. And now there was Donnymania.

Just a few years since playing little dive bars, the Irish rockers have confidently scaled up to huge rooms like this – and are now one of the key interpreters of modern malaise

A mere seven years since their debut, Dogrel, Fontaines DC have enjoyed a virtually seamless passage from Dublin dive bars to arenas, with stadiums to follow next year. Each step has been taken seemingly effortlessly in their stride and this latest outing is no exception. Bathed in shimmering blue light, the band are well into hymnal opener Six Shot Morning before we even see sight of singer Grian Chatten. He wanders on while singing, an entrance worthy of Frank Sinatra.

Chatten has previously seemed to distrust showbiz, but if anything the singer seems far more comfortable on the bigger stage than he ever did on smaller ones. With his Korn T-shirt, unfeasibly baggy trousers and tiny tattoo reading “deadly” in capitals, he leaps around, raises his arms to whip up the crowd and points the microphone towards them to sing key lines. Similarly, music this intense, dark, elegiac and even bleak – which speaks to the void at the heart of much modern life – is hardly typical arena fare but works brilliantly by taking on a more anthemic, celebratory aspect. It’s certainly weirdly thrilling hearing Chatten’s lines such as “We’re all depressed, running on a wheel” or “I don’t feel anything in the modern world” – or a song as plainly dark as Jackie Down the Line – become enormous, arena-uniting sing-songs.
items.t: Fontaines DC review – thrilling gothic grandeur from a band vaulting into greatness
